title: Unit Converter Suite
story: You're planning a trip abroad and every sign, recipe, and speed limit is in different units. Build a portable conversion toolkit so you never need to Google 'how many miles in a kilometer' again.
why: Conversion functions are pure, predictable, and independently useful — the perfect demonstration of functions as reusable building blocks.
analogy: A unit converter is like a currency exchange booth at the airport. You hand them kilometers, they return miles — always at the same rate. The booth clerk (function) doesn't remember you or your previous transactions; they just apply the formula every time.
try_it: Add two temperature conversion functions: `celsius_to_fahrenheit(c: Float64) -> Float64` and `fahrenheit_to_celsius(f: Float64) -> Float64`. The formula is F = C * 9/5 + 32.
tips: Pure functions always return the same output for the same input — no randomness or external state
Use descriptive parameter names: `km` and `miles` tell you exactly what goes in
Round-trip conversions (A->B->A) should give you back roughly the original value
Group related functions together — all distance converters, then all weight converters
common_mistakes: Using Int instead of Float64 — conversions need decimal precision
Using the wrong conversion factor (e.g., miles-to-km factor for km-to-miles)
Forgetting that these are pure functions — they don't modify any external state
